title: Christina Rossetti's birth chart
metaDescription: Christina Rossetti's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 12.9° Sagittarius. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Sun and Mercury sit 0.7° from an exact conjunction — near enough that the tradition reads identity and thinking as a single working part. Two bodies in the same degree are not read as neighbours but as a merger: whatever one wants, the other is already funding.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun's exact place is 12.9° Sagittarius. That falls in the second decan, 10°–20°, sub-ruled by Mars in the classical scheme — a fire sign read through a mutable season.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: The personal planets sit Mercury at 13.6° Sagittarius, Venus at 9.1° Sagittarius, Mars at 3.0° Aries. Mercury in a fire sign reads as a mind that decides at speaking speed; Venus in a fire sign reads as taste that runs toward the vivid and the immediate; Mars in a fire sign reads as drive that ignites on contact.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Uranus and Pluto hold the closest angle here — a sextile, 0.1° wide. The scheme reads a sextile as a door left unlocked. Useful, and entirely dependent on someone walking through it. Behind it, the Sun conjunction Mercury at 0.7°, and Venus trine Pluto at 1.5° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These are the day-proof angles — present at midnight, present at noon, present at the next midnight.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Of the seven planets the classical scheme judges, three sit in a sign it has an opinion about. Mercury in Sagittarius at 13.6° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Mars in Aries at 3.0° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Jupiter in Capricorn at 19.3° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given. Condition, not character: that is all the dignity table ever measured.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Tallied where the signs are certain — 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day — the chart gives fire 5, earth 3, air 1, and mutable 4, cardinal 4, fixed 1 across the modes. No settled placement falls in water — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Pluto was retrograde — the optical reversal the tradition reads as review — energy turned over before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Leo into Virgo during that day at the birthplace, travelling 13.0° between one midnight and the next. Half the day belongs to each sign, and the split falls at an unrecorded hour — so this page holds the Moon as a genuine unknown.
